chunks: We have demonstrated the invalidity of the opinion of those who go to the Imamate of Ja'far ibn Ali from the Fatahiyya, who said regarding the Imamate of Abdullah ibn Ja'far when the Sadiq (peace be upon him) died. And when Abdullah died without leaving a son, they returned to the statement of the Imamate of Musa ibn Ja'far and after him to Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him). And when Hasan (peace be upon him) died, they said regarding the Imamate of Ja'far.

And the statement of these people is invalidated for reasons we invalidated, and because there is no disagreement among the Imamiyyah that the Imamate does not combine in two brothers after Hasan and Husayn, and they have narrated many traditions in that regard.

key_terms.أَخَوَيْنِ: Two brothers, referring to the condition of Imamate not combining in siblings.
key_terms.إِمَامَةُ: Imamate, the doctrine of divine leadership and authority.
key_terms.الْإِمَامِيَّةُ: The Imamiyyah, referring to the Twelver Shia.
key_terms.الْفَطْحِيَّةُ: The Fatahiyya, a Shia sect named after Ja'far ibn Ali (Fath).

ai.seo_question: What is the basis for rejecting the Fatahiyya's claim of Ja'far ibn Ali's Imamate?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi critiques the Fatahiyya sect's shifting allegiance from Abdullah ibn Ja'far to Musa al-Kazim and finally to Ja'far ibn Ali, arguing that their narrative lacks consistency. He grounds his refutation in the established Imami consensus that the Imamate cannot reside in two brothers simultaneously following the era of Hasan and Husayn, a principle supported by numerous hadiths.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: We also demonstrated the invalidity of the promoters of the Imamate of Ja’far Ibn Ali, namely, the Fatahiyya, who believe in the Imamate of Abdullah Ibn Ja’far after the demise of Imam Sadiq (a.s). And when Abdullah passed away without leaving any son, they came back to the Imamate of Musa Ibn Ja’far and after him proclaimed the Imamate of Hasan Ibn Ali. And when Hasan Ibn Ali died, they claimed the Imamate of Ja’far.

Their belief is false for the reasons we invalidated the Imamate of Ja’far Ibn Ali and because there is no disagreement amongst the Imamiyah that Imamate cannot pass from one brother to another after Hasan and Husain and we have brought in that regard great many traditions.
